NL Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch65.R
centrality_nl.Rd

NL centrality (Shao et al. 2019) adds, for each neighbor of a node, the size of the neighbor's two-step neighborhood and the importance of the tie to it: $$NL(v) = \sum_{u \in N(v)} \Bigl(\phi(u) + I_{uv} \frac{k_v - 1}{k_v + k_u - 2}\Bigr),$$ where \(\phi(u)\) is the number of nodes within two steps of \(u\), \(k\) the degree and \(I_{uv}\) the importance of the tie, \((k_u - t - 1)(k_v - t - 1) / (t/2 + 1)\) with \(t\) the number of triangles on it.

Usage

centrality_nl(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The second term is the tie contribution of centrality_dil, so the score equals the sum of \(\phi\) over the neighbors plus that measure minus the degree. \(\phi(u)\) does not count \(u\) itself: the wording and the example of the source list other nodes only, and its tables were not available to test this. The first term carries most of the score. The share of an isolated tie is 0/0 and is taken as 0. Isolated nodes score 0. No published value checks the implementation. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Shao, Z., Liu, S., Zhao, Y. and Liu, Y. (2019). Identifying influential nodes in complex networks based on Neighbours and edges. Peer-to-Peer Networking and Applications, 12, 1528-1537. doi:10.1007/s12083-018-0681-x .

See also

centrality_dil, centrality_lsc, centrality_semilocal, centrality.

Examples

centrality_nl(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   51.86667   65.58081   69.10182   70.64646   57.88571   56.64444   41.71429 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   54.22222   60.70202   49.50222
